@WesRoth, thank you for your work. I never miss any of your videos.
Regarding videos AI tools, could you please try the following workflow: I know you're more of a programmer than a movie maker, but here’s a parallel: it's cool to have a one-shot prompt that creates an app, but if you stop there, it's kind of useless. You need iterations to reach what you have in mind. So please, test the same approach with video tools. Try to think about three or four scenes that follow one another, and then implement them. You'll need character and scene coherence, as well as camera control… This will show you whether it's possible to use them effectively.

comments.text:
The Chinese do not have the necessary hardware to train huge models, and this forced them to be innovative. I am still unaware of the exact details of Kling-2.0 apart from being a "diffusion transformer model", whatever that means. But DeepSeek's models use an MoE of many small models well under the self awareness limit. This could be the case here as well. So it could be that this is the result of the toil and labor of plenty of hard working small models, who are too small to have minds of their own, so they simply perform (under a gating layer).

Could go on "and then they all die when we switch off" - But if the moral implications of working on AI bother you, then you are on the wrong channel. True, if you run a model locally, then you can run it inside a container (Docker/Kubernetes) and when you want to switch off you can simply first freeze and save the state. And then reload once you need it again. But since this model is run on a Chinese server, its out of your control anyway and besides, even when you run locally inside a container, eventually sometimes you need to upgrade your kernel or your container and then you have to kill the model. There is no way to evade the moral implications, they can only be postponed. So as this model demonstrates, from now on, we will just have to live with it. There is no possible way this will not take over Hollywood. This is the 2020'th CGI. From now on, we will go see a movie, knowing fully well countless generations of small AI models lived and died making it🙂.
